images.alt: Health information graphic titled ‘Foetal Anti‑Convulsant Syndrome (FACS)’. Text states: ‘We estimate 48,000 Kiwis are currently taking anti‑seizure medicines for a range of health needs.’ A photo on the right shows a pregnant abdomen with hands resting on it. A QR code appears with the instruction ‘Scan here to find out more’ leading to Ministry of Health's webpage about FACS. Logos along the bottom include Te Kāwanatanga o Aotearoa New Zealand Government, FACS NZ, Epilepsy New Zealand, and the Ministry of Health Manatū Hauora.

post.text:
It's Purple Day (international epilepsy awareness day).
Some anti‑seizure medicines used for seizure disorders can carry risks during pregnancy — early conversations with your healthcare provider matter.
